title: Exact d=2 commutativity certificates for a finite quantum sequential-growth system (Final-Theory Bench v0.3.9)
description: A reproducible exact-symbolic certificate bundle for the repository's frozen n<=4 strong-operator CPOBC compiler. Version 0.3.9 carries forward the v0.3.7 theorem that nonsingular d=2 literal-branch solutions have commuting Q1 through Q4 on the recorded denominator-open locus. The proof remains the Q5-free 21-chart QQ saturation campaign, with two finite-field campaigns retained only as scouts, plus the separate exact scalar-chain identity certificate. Version 0.3.8 changed no scientific verdict: it canonicalised tracked text to LF and supplied a field-aware bridge for 1,007 historical raw-byte bindings to 207 CRLF-era artifacts. Version 0.3.9 likewise changes no scientific verdict: the v0.3 baseline audit resolves the frozen branch through the remote-tracking ref that a full clone with an 'origin' remote provides, so verification no longer depends on a local branch created by hand on the authoring machine. The unrestricted theory remains open. OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, test scaffolding, artifact checks, and prose; Anthropic Claude assisted with research design, the Q5-free proof strategy, symbolic cross-checks, and prior-art review, and in v0.3.9 additionally wrote the deterministic deposit-archive builder, its regression tests, and the release and reproduction prose accompanying them. No AI system contributed a proof-bearing claim that is not tied to an exact, inspectable artifact and its tests. The human author selected the scope and resource budgets, reviewed the work, and remains responsible for every claim; AI systems are not authors. The v0.3.7 short report in this bundle, and the other artifacts frozen before this release, carry the author name To-Marigi, a handle of the same author, recorded as an alternative name on ORCID 0009-0003-9256-7089. Those artifacts are frozen: their recorded SHA-256 digests are left valid rather than rewritten, which is why the earlier name still appears inside them. This deposit is a curated bundle of the 205 files named by results/v0.3.9_release_manifest.json plus that manifest, 206 files in total, and is not a repository snapshot. Third-party material is deliberately excluded and is not covered by the MIT licence: the 52 PDFs under references/papers/, the 52 texts extracted from them under references/text/, and the 3 vendored archives under oracle/sage_periods/vendor/. The provenance records for all of it are included in this bundle. references/manifest.json gives each archived paper its arXiv identifier, URL, byte size, page count and SHA-256, and names the text extracted from it; references/sources.json is the catalogue those records index, covering 59 works including the 7 for which no PDF was archived; oracle/sage_periods/source_manifest.json gives each vendored archive its upstream repository, commit and SHA-256, together with the SageMath container digest. The papers and the vendored archives can therefore be fetched from their sources and checked against the recorded digests. The extracted texts carry no separate digest and are reproduced by re-extracting from the corresponding PDF. No reference record carries a licence field for any entry, which is why none of this material is redistributed here. Full verification additionally requires the git repository, because the baseline audits resolve commits, tags and a branch; see REPRODUCING_v0.3.9.md.
